title: P0: Hosted API abrupt multiplex backpressure surge — investigation notes & runbook draft
content:
Executive summary:

On 2027-02-18 02:32 UTC we observed a sudden, system-wide degradation affecting streaming responses on the Hosted API. Symptoms included a rapid increase in streaming 5xx errors, sustained tail-latency growth (P95/P99), and a correlated rise in connection-level backpressure metrics. The incident lasted ~47 minutes of customer-visible impact; mitigations restored normal service at ~03:19 UTC.

Impact:
- Affected surface: streaming endpoints (multiplexed sessions) for the Hosted API. Non-streaming (batch generation) endpoints mostly unaffected.
- Client-visible: increased streaming disconnects and 5xx responses, partial message truncation for long-lived sessions.
- Scope: ~18% of active streaming sessions saw elevated error rates; top 10 customers accounted for 62% of errors.
- Duration: 02:32 UTC -> 03:19 UTC (mitigation enacted at 02:45 UTC, full normalization by 03:19 UTC).

Detection timeline (high level):
- 02:29 UTC: internal streaming error-rate alert (SRE streaming-5xx-rate) fires (on-call).
- 02:32 UTC: Ops console shows cluster-level acceptor queue length rising on edge nodes in us-west1 and eu-west1.
- 02:35 UTC: Telemetry shows spike in per-connection write queue and KV-cache eviction spikes for multiplexing-worker pods.
- 02:40 UTC: On-call creates incident channel and begins triage; triage indicates correlation with a recent runtime push (PR #1842 deployed 02:15 UTC).
- 02:45 UTC: Emergency mitigation: route new streaming sessions away from affected acceptance nodes + apply temporary per-connection throughput cap (20kb/s) and emergency per-prefix throttle for top 5 customers. 5xx rate drops but tail latency remains elevated.
- 03:10 UTC: Rollback of PR #1842 in non-critical clusters shows latency normalization; deploy configuration tweak to multiplexer (circuit-breaker heuristic) to reduce headroom depletion.
- 03:19 UTC: Metrics return to expected baselines; incident declared mitigated.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
A change in the serving runtime (PR #1842) altered internal multiplexing scheduling heuristics intended to improve fairness for low-throughput sessions. Under real traffic patterns (several heavy, long-lived streaming clients with interleaved small sessions), the new scheduler allowed headroom starvation on acceptor threads. Starvation led to a buildup of in-memory write queues and accelerated KV cache evictions. Excessive eviction churn caused worker stalls and increased synchronous disk/serialization calls in a few code paths, producing backpressure that propagated to acceptors and resulted in elevated 5xx and disconnects.

Contributing factors:
- The PR changed scheduling without an end-to-end load test covering multiplexed long-tail workloads.
- Autoscaler thresholds were tuned for throughput rather than connection-level write-queue depth; autoscaler reacted too slowly.
- No circuit-breaker/backpressure-shedding existed for the multiplexed worker; failure mode amplified across pods.
- Top customers' session patterns (very long-lived + bursts) were not represented in internal synthetic tests.

Evidence & metrics used during RCA:
- Streaming-5xx-rate (svc/hosted-api) time series shows spike from 0.2% -> 4.7% at 02:32 UTC.
- Acceptors: ephemeral-acceptor-queue-length (P99) rose from 30 -> 420 per node at peak.
- Multiplexing-worker write_queue_len median -> 95ms to 1200ms processing latency; tailed P99->3.4s.
- KV-cache eviction rate increased 8x during incident window; memory churn on affected pods increased by ~22%.
- Relevant deploy: serving-runtime@sha:3a7f2b (PR #1842) rolled out at 02:15 UTC.

PromQL / psuedo queries used:
- rate(http_server_errors_total{route=~"/stream.*"}[1m])  - to track streaming 5xx spike.
- histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(multiplex_worker_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le)) - to see tail latency.
- sum(increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (pod) - to find eviction hotspots.

Immediate mitigations executed (timeline & owners):
- 02:45 UTC: Route new streaming sessions away from affected edge acceptor pools (On-call: Maya Chen).
- 02:50 UTC: Apply emergency per-connection throughput cap in env var config for streaming gateway (On-call: Noah Kim).
- 02:55 UTC: Apply per-customer temporary throttle (top 5 customers) via routing policy (Owner: SRE / Solutions Eng).
- 03:05 UTC: Start controlled rollback test of PR #1842 in staging-like cluster; rollback confirmed improvement (Owner: Liam O'Neill).
- 03:12 UTC: Deploy conservative multiplexing config (lower concurrency threshold + simple circuit-breaker) to affected clusters (Owner: Platform Eng).

Post-incident mitigation actions (short-term):
- Revert the scheduling change from PR #1842 across all regions until a safe variant is validated (Owner: Serving Runtime SE, target: 2027-02-24).
- Expand monitoring: add per-connection write queue depth alert and a reconstructed metric for multiplexer headroom (Owner: Observability, target: 2027-02-22).
- Add a temporary pre-deploy check that runs a synthetic multiplexed workload with long-lived sessions (Owner: Release Eng, target: 2027-02-28).

Permanent fix candidates and roadmap (longer-term):
1) Implement a per-multiplexer circuit breaker that can proactively shed or backoff lower-priority streams when headroom falls below threshold (Owner: Serving Runtime, ETA: 2 sprints).
2) Revise autoscaler to consider connection-level backpressure signals (write_queue_len, headroom) not just CPU/RPS (Owner: Platform Eng, ETA: 3–4 sprints).
3) Rework scheduling heuristics to be latency-safe by design and add canary tests that simulate the long-lived session patterns from our top customers (Owner: Applied ML / Runtime, ETA: 3 sprints).
4) Add a mitigation hook in the control plane to automatically route new sessions to a fallback pool if per-node headroom crosses emergency threshold (Owner: Console + Platform Eng, ETA: 4 sprints).

Runbook draft for 'streaming-multiplexer-backpressure' (quick steps for on-call):
1) Verify alert and scope: query streaming-5xx-rate and per-node acceptor-queue length to confirm pattern.
2) Identify hotspots: run "sum by(node)(increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]))" and sort.
3) Temporary routing: use console -> routing -> session-placement to avoid nodes with acceptor_queue_len > 200 (manual step).
4) Apply soft throttles: set STREAM_CONN_THROUGHPUT_LIMIT to 20kb/s as a feature-flagged emergency config.
5) Apply per-customer throttles for top offenders (console routing).
6) If recent deploy suspected: immediately rollback to previous serving-runtime SHA for the cluster(s) showing the highest headroom depletion.
7) If rollback not possible: scale up acceptor pool by 30% and enable conservative multiplexing config (circuit-breaker ON).
8) Post-incident: capture traces for a 10-minute window (request IDs) and attach to incident ticket.

Runbook notes / caveats:
- Manual routing changes are delicate; ensure changes are targeted (avoid global shifts).
- Per-customer throttles require pre-approved billing/CS outreach for top customers; prefer temporary rate-limits rather than session drops.
- Circuit-breaker behavior must be explained to the on-call so they can reason about client disconnects vs graceful backoff.

Action items (owners, status, due):
- Serving Runtime: create unit test + integration harness for multiplexed long-lived sessions; PR by 2027-03-05 (Owner: Liam O'Neill) [in_progress].
- Observability: add headroom metric and alert; PR / dashboards by 2027-02-22 (Owner: Aisha Gomez) [todo].
- Release Eng: add synthetic multiplexed job to preflight suite; complete by 2027-02-28 (Owner: Release Eng) [todo].
- Platform Eng: proposal for autoscaler change to include write_queue_len; draft by 2027-03-08 (Owner: Noah Kim) [todo].
- Customer Success: notify top 5 impacted customers with incident summary and mitigation plan by 2027-02-22 (Owner: CS lead) [todo].

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did the autoscaler not add capacity earlier? Need timeline of scaling events vs headroom drop.
- How representative are our synthetic workloads of top customers? Need sampling + replay plan.
- Did any other recent PRs change KV cache eviction heuristics? Cross-check PR history.

Notes to self (on-call playbook edits):
- Add explicit checklist to check for recent merges with "multiplex" or "scheduler" tags.
- Shorten detection sliding window from 5m->2m for streaming 5xx alerts.
- Add a preapproved temporary throttling policy for the largest customers to avoid manual CS signoff during P0.

Appendix (artifacts and links):
- Deployed SHA: serving-runtime@3a7f2b; rollback target: serving-runtime@2f4b1d.
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-5238.
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1842
- Dashboards: internal link (confluence entry in linked_artifacts).

Summary of learning: this incident highlights risk of scheduler changes without end-to-end, customer-pattern-aware preflight tests, and the need for headroom-aware autoscaling and circuit-breakers in the multiplexing path. The temporary mitigations (routing, throttles, rollback) were effective; the long-term fix requires changes across runtime, autoscaling, and release engineering.

Prepared by: Ravi Patel (on-call SRE), with contributions from Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill, Aisha Gomez, Noah Kim.

Status: draft RCA and runbook — ready for engineering review and prioritization in next SRE triage meeting.
